requirements.title: Library statistics
requirements.rationale: The owner sees the size and shape of the whole library in one answer.

criteria.action: answer with the library, content, topics, tags, workspaces and hosts sections computed over the signed-in owner's links at the time of the request
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with a JSON object holding library {total, by_state {pending, active, unreachable, expired, archived}, pinned, in_workspace, limit: 20000}, content {by_kind {html, pdf, other, unfetched}, with_snapshot, reader_empty}, topics {total, by_level {"1", "2", "3"}, links_without_topic, largest}, tags {total, used_once, links_without_tags, top}, workspaces {total, largest} and hosts {distinct, top}

check.pseudocode: in src/worker/stats/stats.test.ts, a new describe 'library statistics': seed links through seedLinks in each state (2 pending, 3 active, 1 unreachable, 1 expired, 1 archived), pin one, put one in a workspace, set content_kind html/pdf/other/null and has_snapshot/reader_empty on some, file links under a level-1, level-2 and level-3 topic (placeTopic), tag them; r = api GET /api/v1/stats; assert r.status == 200; assert r.json.library == {total: 8, by_state: {pending: 2, active: 3, unreachable: 1, expired: 1, archived: 1}, pinned: 1, in_workspace: 1, limit: 20000}; assert content.by_kind, with_snapshot, reader_empty, topics.total, topics.by_level {'1','2','3'}, links_without_topic, tags.total, tags.used_once, links_without_tags, workspaces.total and hosts.distinct equal the seeded numbers

criteria.action: for any library, present every key of library.by_state and content.by_kind even when its count is 0, with the by_state values adding up to library.total

check.pseudocode: in src/worker/stats/stats.test.ts in 'library statistics', a table over the libraries {no links, only active links, one link in each state}: r = GET /api/v1/stats; assert Object.keys(r.json.library.by_state) == the five states and Object.keys(r.json.content.by_kind) == html, pdf, other, unfetched; assert the sum of by_state == library.total

criteria.condition: the owner has no links, topics, tags or workspaces
criteria.action: answer with every count at 0 and every list (topics.largest, tags.top, workspaces.largest, hosts.top) empty
criteria.contract: HTTP 200; every count 0 except library.limit (20000); every list []

check.pseudocode: in src/worker/stats/stats.test.ts in 'library statistics': a newly signed-in owner; r = GET /api/v1/stats; assert r.status == 200, every number in library, content, topics, tags, workspaces and hosts is 0 except library.limit, and every list is []

criteria.action: count only the signed-in owner's links, topics, tags, workspaces, imports, vectors and history, never another user's

check.pseudocode: in src/worker/stats/stats.test.ts in 'library statistics': owner A and owner B (signIn with two emails) each seed links, topics, tags and a workspace; r = GET /api/v1/stats as A; assert every count equals A's seeded numbers and no list holds an id or name of B's

criteria.action: list in topics.largest the 10 topics with the most links filed directly under them as {id, name, path, count}, in tags.top the 10 tags on the most links as {id, name, count}, in workspaces.largest the 10 workspaces with the most links as {id, name, count} and in hosts.top the 10 hosts with the most links as {host, count}, each by count descending with ties broken by name or host A to Z

check.pseudocode: in src/worker/stats/stats.test.ts in 'library statistics': seed 11 tags where two share the 10th place count ('beta' and 'alpha'), 11 topics with one under a parent, 11 workspaces and 11 hosts the same way; r = GET /api/v1/stats; assert each list has 10 entries in count order, 'alpha' is listed and 'beta' is not, and the child topic's path is [parent name, child name]

requirements.title: Expiry outlook
requirements.rationale: The owner sees which links decay will expire or remove next, before it happens.

criteria.action: count in expiry.expiring the unprotected links (state active, pending or unreachable, not pinned, in no workspace) at 0 points or below as today, at 1 to 7 points as within_7_days and at 8 to 30 points as within_30_days, with points computed by pointsAt at the time of the request
criteria.contract: expiry.expiring == {today, within_7_days, within_30_days}; the buckets do not overlap

check.pseudocode: in src/worker/stats/stats.test.ts, a new describe 'expiry outlook', a table over (start points 60, use count, last used days ago) giving points -1, 0, 1, 7, 8, 30, 31: setNow; seed one unprotected active link per row, plus a pinned link and a workspace link at 0 points and an archived link; r = GET /api/v1/stats; assert r.json.expiry.expiring == {today: 2, within_7_days: 2, within_30_days: 2}; for each seeded link assert its bucket agrees with the decay_note GET /api/v1/links/{id} returns ('expires today', 'expires in N days')

criteria.action: list in expiry.points_histogram the unprotected links in the point ranges ≤0, 1–7, 8–30, 31–60, 61–90 and >90, in that order, every range present
criteria.contract: an array of exactly six {range, count} objects in the order ≤0, 1–7, 8–30, 31–60, 61–90, >90

check.pseudocode: in src/worker/stats/stats.test.ts in 'expiry outlook', with the table of REQ-2.1 plus links at 60, 61, 90 and 91 points: assert r.json.expiry.points_histogram == [{range: '≤0', count: 2}, {range: '1–7', count: 2}, {range: '8–30', count: 2}, {range: '31–60', count: 2}, {range: '61–90', count: 2}, {range: '>90', count: 1}]; with no links every count is 0 and all six ranges are present

criteria.action: count in expiry.protected_at_risk the links that are pinned or in a workspace, in neither the expired nor the archived state, at 0 points or below

check.pseudocode: in src/worker/stats/stats.test.ts in 'expiry outlook': seed a pinned link at -3 points, a workspace link at 0 points, a pinned link at 5 points, an expired pinned link and an archived link at old last use; assert r.json.expiry.protected_at_risk == 2

criteria.action: count in expiry.awaiting_removal the expired links that are neither pinned nor in a workspace as total, and those whose removal_at (expired_at plus remove_days) is within 7 and within 30 days of the request as within_7_days and within_30_days, cumulatively, a removal_at already past counting in both

check.pseudocode: in src/worker/stats/stats.test.ts in 'expiry outlook', remove_days 180: seed expired links whose removal_at is 1 day ago, in 3 days, in 20 days and in 100 days, and an expired pinned link; assert r.json.expiry.awaiting_removal == {total: 4, within_7_days: 2, within_30_days: 3}

criteria.action: give in expiry.settings the owner's start_points and remove_days

check.pseudocode: in src/worker/stats/stats.test.ts in 'expiry outlook': PUT /api/v1/settings/decay to start points 30 and remove days 90; assert r.json.expiry.settings == {start_points: 30, remove_days: 90}

requirements.title: Health
requirements.rationale: The owner sees links that are broken or stuck, and why.

criteria.action: give in health.unreachable the number of links in state unreachable and by_reason, the 5 most common state_reason values among them as [{reason, count}] by count descending with ties broken by reason A to Z
criteria.contract: health.unreachable == {count, by_reason: [{reason, count}] of at most 5}

check.pseudocode: in src/worker/stats/stats.test.ts, a new describe 'health': seed unreachable links with 6 distinct reasons ('HTTP 503' ×3, 'timed out' ×2, four others once each); assert r.json.health.unreachable == {count: 9, by_reason: 5 entries starting [{reason: 'HTTP 503', count: 3}, {reason: 'timed out', count: 2}] then three of the single reasons A to Z}

criteria.action: give in health.dead the number of links with one or more consecutive failed liveness checks and dead_over_30_days, those whose dead_since is 30 or more days before the request

check.pseudocode: in src/worker/stats/stats.test.ts in 'health': seed links with liveness_failures 0, 1 (dead_since 2 days ago) and 3 (dead_since 30 days ago); assert r.json.health.dead == {count: 2, dead_over_30_days: 1}

criteria.action: give in health.enrichment the number of links in each enrichment status no_key, queued, enriched, failed, skipped and waiting_for_key, and none for a null status, every key present, and failed_by_reason, the 5 most common enrichment_reason values among failed links as [{reason, count}] ordered as in REQ-3.1

check.pseudocode: in src/worker/stats/stats.test.ts in 'health': seed one link in each enrichment status, two failed with reason 'provider_failed' and a pending link with a null status; assert r.json.health.enrichment == {no_key: 1, queued: 1, enriched: 1, failed: 3, skipped: 1, waiting_for_key: 1, none: 1, failed_by_reason: [{reason: 'provider_failed', count: 2}, ...]}

criteria.action: give in health.ai_key the owner's AI key status: none without a stored key, verified, or rejected

check.pseudocode: in src/worker/stats/stats.test.ts in 'health', a table over {no key: 'none', a key FakeAi accepts: 'verified', a key FakeAi rejects: 'rejected'}: store the key through PUT /api/v1/settings/ai as src/worker/enrich/keys.test.ts does; assert r.json.health.ai_key == the expected status

requirements.title: Background backlog
requirements.rationale: The owner sees whether background work is keeping up, from what the database records as waiting.

criteria.action: give in backlog.fetch_pending the links in state pending, in backlog.fetch_retrying those of them with one or more failed fetch attempts, and in backlog.enrichment_queued the links whose enrichment status is queued

check.pseudocode: in src/worker/stats/stats.test.ts, a new describe 'background backlog': seed 3 pending links, one with fetch_attempts 2, and 2 links with enrichment_status queued; assert r.json.backlog.fetch_pending == 3, fetch_retrying == 1 and enrichment_queued == 2

criteria.action: list in backlog.imports the owner's imports that have links waiting or in progress, newest first, at most 10, each as {id, created_at, added, waiting, in_progress, done} with the numbers GET /api/v1/imports/{id} reports in its progress
criteria.contract: backlog.imports: at most 10 {id, created_at, added, waiting, in_progress, done}, newest first; an import with nothing waiting or in progress is absent

check.pseudocode: in src/worker/stats/stats.test.ts in 'background backlog': import 12 files through POST /api/v1/imports (no every-minute run, so their links wait) and one more whose links are all fetched (deliverFetches); assert backlog.imports has 10 entries, the newest first, none of them the finished import; for the first, assert waiting, in_progress and done equal GET /api/v1/imports/{id}'s progress

criteria.action: give in backlog.index_stale the owner's links whose meaning index is stale (no passage carries the link's current text version) and in backlog.vector_deletions the owner's vectors waiting to be deleted

check.pseudocode: in src/worker/stats/stats.test.ts in 'background backlog': add two links and index one of them (deliverIndexing) and change the other's note; insert two vector_deletions rows for the owner and one for another user; assert backlog.index_stale == 1 and backlog.vector_deletions == 2

criteria.action: give in backlog.liveness_due the owner's links the next hourly run would enqueue for a liveness check: neither expired nor archived, active or pinned, last checked (or never checked and added) 7 or more days before the request, and not enqueued in the last 6 hours

check.pseudocode: in src/worker/stats/stats.test.ts in 'background backlog', a table over {active and checked 8 days ago: due, active and checked 2 days ago: not due, pinned pending never checked and added 8 days ago: due, active checked 8 days ago and enqueued 1 hour ago: not due, expired: not due, archived: not due}: assert backlog.liveness_due == 2; then run the hourly run (runScheduled in src/worker/decay/cron.ts) with recordLivenessQueue and assert it enqueued exactly the links counted

criteria.action: give in backlog.throttle_clear_at the later of the owner's throttle_next_at and import_window_end as an ISO 8601 time, or null when that time is not after the request
criteria.contract: backlog.throttle_clear_at: an ISO 8601 string or null

check.pseudocode: in src/worker/stats/stats.test.ts in 'background backlog', a table over (throttle_next_at, import_window_end) = (now + 12 min, null), (now + 1 min, now + 5 min), (now - 1 min, null), (null, null): set the users row; assert backlog.throttle_clear_at == now + 12 min, now + 5 min, null and null as ISO strings

requirements.title: Activity from history
requirements.rationale: The owner sees what happened in the library over the last 30 days, from the history it keeps.

criteria.action: list in activity.added_per_day the links added and in activity.uses_per_day the uses recorded on each of the last 30 UTC days, today included, oldest first, one {day: 'YYYY-MM-DD', count} per day including days with 0
criteria.contract: two arrays of exactly 30 {day, count}, oldest first, the last day today in UTC

check.pseudocode: in src/worker/stats/stats.test.ts, a new describe 'activity': setNow('2026-11-10T00:30:00Z'); seed links added at 2026-11-10T00:10Z, 2026-11-09T23:50Z (twice) and 2026-10-11T23:59Z and 2026-10-12T00:00Z; record uses on two of them on 2026-11-09; r = GET /api/v1/stats; assert added_per_day has 30 entries from '2026-10-12' to '2026-11-10', entry '2026-10-12' == 1, '2026-11-09' == 2, '2026-11-10' == 1 and every other 0; assert uses_per_day '2026-11-09' == 2

criteria.action: give in activity.added_last_7_days and activity.added_last_30_days the links added in the last 7 and 30 UTC days, today included

list in activity.most_used the 10 links with the most uses in the last 30 days as {id, title, host, uses}, by uses descending, ties broken by the most recent use first, and give in activity.never_used the links whose use count is 0

check.pseudocode: in src/worker/stats/stats.test.ts in 'activity': seed 12 links, record uses so that two tie on 3 uses (the later used last yesterday), one has uses only 31 days ago and two have none; assert most_used has 10 entries, the tied pair ordered later-use first, the link used only 31 days ago absent; assert never_used == 2

criteria.action: give in activity.fetches the ok and failed fetch attempts recorded in the last 30 days and failed_by_reason, the 5 most common reasons of the failed ones, ordered as in REQ-3.1

check.pseudocode: in src/worker/stats/stats.test.ts in 'activity': insert link_events rows of kind 'fetch' (3 ok, 2 failed 'HTTP 503' within 30 days, 1 failed 40 days ago); assert activity.fetches == {ok: 3, failed: 2, failed_by_reason: [{reason: 'HTTP 503', count: 2}]}

criteria.action: list in activity.imports the owner's last 10 imports, newest first, each as {id, created_at, url_lines, added, duplicates, invalid, not_imported}
criteria.contract: activity.imports: at most 10 {id, created_at, url_lines, added, duplicates, invalid, not_imported}, newest first

check.pseudocode: in src/worker/stats/stats.test.ts in 'activity': make 11 imports through POST /api/v1/imports with known counts; assert activity.imports has 10 entries, newest first, each with the counts its POST answered

requirements.title: The stats API's behaviour
requirements.rationale: The statistics are as private, cheap and dependable as every other route.

criteria.condition: GET /api/v1/stats arrives with no valid session or token
criteria.action: answer as every route under /api/v1/ answers without credentials, computing nothing

check.pseudocode: in src/worker/stats/stats.test.ts, a new describe 'the stats route': r = GET /api/v1/stats without a session or token; assert r.status == 401 and r.json == {error: 'unauthorized'}; with a bearer token from createToken the answer is 200

criteria.action: change no row of any table when answering GET /api/v1/stats, and ignore any query parameter

check.pseudocode: in src/worker/stats/stats.test.ts in 'the stats route': seed a library with pending, expired and liveness-due links and an import; snapshot every row of links, users, imports, import_links and link_index_state; r1 = GET /api/v1/stats; r2 = GET /api/v1/stats?days=7&x=1; assert the snapshot is unchanged and r1.json == r2.json

criteria.action: describe GET /api/v1/stats and its 200 and 401 answers in the OpenAPI document served at GET /api/v1/openapi.json

check.pseudocode: src/worker/api/openapi.test.ts already fails when a registered route is missing from the document or a response the tests receive is not declared; the stats tests' responses are checked by it once the route is registered

criteria.condition: the owner's library holds 20,000 links, with 20,000 uses and 20,000 fetch events in the last 30 days
criteria.action: answer within 2 seconds
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 within 2,000 ms in the Worker tests

check.pseudocode: in src/worker/stats/stats.test.ts in 'the stats route': seedLinks 20,000 links across all states with hosts, topics and tags; insert 20,000 link_uses and 20,000 link_events rows within the last 30 days; t0 = Date.now(); r = GET /api/v1/stats; assert r.status == 200, r.json.library.total == 20000 and Date.now() - t0 <= 2000

criteria.condition: computing any section of the statistics fails
criteria.action: answer with an internal error and no partial result

check.pseudocode: in src/worker/stats/stats.test.ts in 'the stats route': through a test hook on the stats computation (as decayHooks does for decay), make one section's query throw; r = GET /api/v1/stats; assert r.status == 500 and r.json == {error: 'internal'}

requirements.title: The Stats page
requirements.rationale: The owner reads the statistics on one page and goes from a number to the links it counts.

criteria.action: show a Stats tab with its own icon between the Archive and Settings tabs of the navigation, opening /stats, with the breadcrumb reading 'Stats' there

check.pseudocode: in src/web/pages/Stats.test.tsx, a new describe 'Stats page': renderPage('/stats', FakeApi answering GET /api/v1/stats); tabs = the links of the navigation named 'Sections'; assert tabs.indexOf('Stats') == tabs.indexOf('Archive') + 1 and tabs.indexOf('Settings') == tabs.indexOf('Stats') + 1; assert the Stats tab is aria-current='page' and the breadcrumb shows 'Stats' (as src/web/pages/Archive.test.tsx checks its tab)

criteria.action: request GET /api/v1/stats once, show a spinner until the answer arrives, then show the sections Library, Expiry, Background work, Health and Activity in that order with the answer's numbers; request it again when the owner presses Refresh, and never on its own

check.pseudocode: in src/web/pages/Stats.test.tsx in 'Stats page': FakeApi answers GET /api/v1/stats with a fixed body after a delay; renderPage('/stats'); assert a spinner is shown, then the five headings in order and numbers from the body (library total, expired count, fetch_pending); assert api.sent('GET', '/api/v1/stats').length == 1; advance fake timers by 10 minutes and assert it is still 1; press Refresh and assert it is 2

criteria.action: link each count to the page listing what it counts where one exists: the expired count to /expired, the archived count to /archive, a topic to its topic: search, a tag to its tag: search, a workspace to its page, an import to its report GET /api/v1/imports/{id}/report and a most-used link to its detail page

check.pseudocode: in src/web/pages/Stats.test.tsx in 'Stats page': with a body holding one of each; assert the expired count's link href == '/expired', the archived count's == '/archive', the topic's == searchPath(filterQuery('topic', name)), the tag's == searchPath(filterQuery('tag', name)), the workspace's == '/workspaces/' + id, the import's == '/api/v1/imports/' + id + '/report' and the most-used link's == '/links/' + id

criteria.action: draw activity.added_per_day, activity.uses_per_day and expiry.points_histogram as bar charts with one bar per entry, whose tooltip gives the entry's day or range and its count, each beside a table of the same numbers that screen readers can read, with no charting library

check.pseudocode: in src/web/pages/Stats.test.tsx in 'Stats page': with a 30-day series where one day is 4; assert the 'Added per day' chart has 30 bars, the bar for that day has a title '2026-11-09: 4'; assert a table (visually hidden) with 30 rows holds the same days and counts; the histogram has 6 bars in range order

criteria.action: show each list's empty state when it is empty ('No topics yet', 'No tags yet', 'No workspaces yet', 'No imports yet'), under each activity series the caption 'counts only links still in your library', and a throttle_clear_at in the future as 'background work clears in about N minutes', rounded up to the whole minute, or 'background work is idle' when it is null

check.pseudocode: in src/web/pages/Stats.test.tsx in 'Stats page', a table over bodies {every list empty and throttle_clear_at null, throttle_clear_at 11 min 20 s after the fake now}: assert the four empty-state texts and 'background work is idle' for the first; 'background work clears in about 12 minutes' for the second; the activity caption is shown under each series

criteria.condition: GET /api/v1/stats fails or answers with an error status
criteria.action: show 'Couldn't load statistics' and a Try again button in the error style of the other pages, which requests GET /api/v1/stats again
criteria.contract: the page shows "Couldn't load statistics" and a Try again button, and no section

check.pseudocode: in src/web/pages/Stats.test.tsx in 'Stats page': FakeApi answers GET /api/v1/stats with 500 {error: 'internal'} then 200; renderPage('/stats'); assert the text "Couldn't load statistics" and no section heading; press Try again; assert the Library section is shown

execution_paths.title: The owner adds links and sees them counted

steps.action: adds three links through the website
fetches each link from the fake origin and makes it active
computes the statistics over the owner's links and answers
shows 3 links, 3 active, and today's bar in Added per day at 3

setup: wrangler dev with the fake origin and fake Google provider, as make e2e runs
end_state: the Library section shows a total of 3 and 3 active
today's bar in Added per day has the tooltip '<today>: 3'
smoke.pseudocode: in a new e2e/stats.spec.ts: signIn(page); addLinks(page, three fake-origin URLs); wait until the stream shows them fetched; click the 'Stats' tab; expect the Library total 3 and active 3; expect the last bar of 'Added per day' to have the title '<today>: 3'

execution_paths.title: A link reaches 0 points, decay expires it, and the owner follows the count

steps.action: opens Stats with one link last used 61 days ago at 60 start points
runs the hourly decay run, which expires the link
presses Refresh and then the expired count
shows 1 expired and opens the Expired page listing the link

setup: one link whose last_used_at is set to daysAgo(61) through d1()
end_state: Stats shows 1 under 'expires today' before the run and 1 expired after it
the Expired page lists the link
smoke.pseudocode: in e2e/stats.spec.ts: signIn; addLinkIds one URL; d1(UPDATE links SET last_used_at = daysAgo(61)); goto /stats; expect 'expires today' 1; runScheduled(page); click Refresh; expect expired 1; click the expired count; expect the URL /expired and the link's card

execution_paths.title: An import shows in the backlog until it is done

steps.action: imports a file of 50 fake-origin URLs on the Import page
lists the import in backlog.imports with links waiting
runs the every-minute dispatch until every link is sent
after Refresh, no longer lists the import under Background work and lists it under Activity's imports with 50 added

setup: the fake origin answers every imported URL
end_state: before the dispatch the import is listed under Background work with 50 waiting
after it the import is absent from Background work and listed in Activity's imports with 50 added
smoke.pseudocode: in e2e/stats.spec.ts, after the pattern of e2e/import.spec.ts: signIn; import a 50-line file; goto /stats; expect the import under Background work with 50 waiting; runMinute(page) and advance until the import's progress has nothing waiting or in progress; click Refresh; expect it absent from Background work and listed under Activity with 50 added
